items.title: A set symmetric for a sparse statistic is Schur-positive with an explicit two-row expansion
items.author: Avichai Marmor
items.work: Schur-positivity of short chords in matchings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:if two rows and symmetric then schur positive` at source lines 612-618: if A is symmetric for a sparse statistic D then A is Schur-positive, with the explicit expansion Q_D(A) = sum over k of |A(D = odds(k))| s_{N-k,k}. The author's proof (source lines 619-642) is a multi-stage argument rather than a formal consequence of the criterion: it converts symmetry into the generating-function identity (lines 620-623), selects a Schur coefficient maximal in the conjugate order (line 626), evaluates the refined identity at the descent set of the corresponding superstandard tableau (lines 628-632) and uses the first superstandard characterisation to conclude that this coefficient is exactly |A(D = Des(T_mu))| and non-zero (lines 632-633). The key structural step is at lines 634-635, where sparsity of D(a) together with the appearance of {1,2} in Des(T_mu) forces the shape to have at most two parts and kills every other coefficient; only then does the two-row characterisation identify the remaining coefficients (line 641).
